title: Ruby Laser
short_intro: The ruby laser is a solid-state three-level laser that uses a synthetic ruby rod as the active medium and produces coherent red light at a wavelength of 694.3 nm. Optical pumping via a high-intensity flashlamp is employed to achieve population inversion between the excited and ground energy states of chromium ions.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Basic working principle, identification of active medium (Cr<sup>3+</sup> in Al<sub>2<sub>3</sub></sub>), pump source (xenon flashlamp), and emission wavelength (694.3 nm).
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Detailed energy level kinetics of a three-level laser system, threshold pump power derivation, rate equations for population densities, and optical resonator cavity modes.

prerequisites: Energy levels of atoms and ions

concept_notes.heading: Active Medium and Crystal Structure
bullets: The active medium of a ruby laser consists of a synthetic sapphire crystal (aluminum oxide, Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) doped with approximately 0.05% by weight of trivalent chromium ions (Cr<sup>3+</sup>).

The host Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> lattice is optically transparent and mechanically robust, while the Cr<sup>3+</sup> ions provide the active optical transition responsible for fluorescence and laser action.
The chromium ions substitute for aluminum ions in the crystal lattice, experiencing a strong crystalline electric field that splits their d-orbitals.

concept_notes.heading: Three-Level Energy Scheme
bullets: The ruby laser operates on a three-level laser system comprising the ground state (E<sub>1</sub>), a broad pump band (E<sub>3</sub>), and a metastable upper laser level (E<sub>2</sub>).
Optical pumping excites Cr<sup>3+</sup> ions from E<sub>1</sub> to the broad absorption bands E<sub>3</sub> using intense green and blue light from a xenon flashlamp.
From E<sub>3</sub>, the ions undergo rapid, non-radiative radiationless transitions (phonon relaxation) to the metastable level E<sub>2</sub> with a lifetime of approximately 3 ms.

concept_notes.heading: Optical Resonator and Feedback
bullets: The ruby rod has its ends flat, parallel, highly polished, and coated with reflective films to form a Fabry-Perot optical cavity.
One end mirror is total reflecting (>99% reflectivity), while the output coupler mirror is partially reflecting (typically 70-80% reflectivity) to allow laser beam extraction.
Photons bouncing back and forth along the axis stimulate emission from the E<sub>2</sub> to E<sub>1</sub> transition, building up an intense, highly directional coherent beam.

concept_notes.heading: Pulsed Operation Characteristics
bullets: Because the lower laser level is the ground state (E<sub>1</sub>), more than 50% of the total chromium ions must be excited to the metastable state E<sub>2</sub> to achieve population inversion.
This high pumping threshold requires very intense optical pumping, making continuous-wave (CW) operation extremely difficult; thus, ruby lasers typically operate in pulsed mode.
The output appears as a train of intense microsecond spikes corresponding to dynamic gain switching within the resonator cavity.

derivations.title: Threshold Population Inversion Density
derivations.conditions: Steady-state operation of a three-level laser medium with cavity length L and mirror reflectivities R<sub>1</sub> and R<sub>2</sub>
steps: Write the condition for net optical gain per unit length: gamma(\nu) = \sigma(\nu)(N_2 - N_1) \ge \alpha_{int} + \frac{1}{2L}\ln\left(\frac{1}{R_1 R_2}\right), where \sigma is the stimulated emission cross-section and \alpha_{int} is internal cavity loss.
For a three-level system where the lower level is the ground state, let total ion density be N_t = N_1 + N_2.
At threshold, set the net gain equal to the total cavity loss coefficient \alpha_{th} = \alpha_{int} + \frac{1}{2L}\ln\left(\frac{1}{R_1 R_2}\right).
Substitute N_1 = N_t - N_2 into the gain equation to solve for the threshold population inversion density (N_2 - N_1)_{th}.

derivations.title: Threshold Pump Power Rate
derivations.conditions: Three-level system with pump band lifetime \tau_{31} \ll \tau_{21} and pumping rate W_{13}
steps: Consider the rate equation for the upper laser level population density N_2: \frac{dN_2}{dt} = W_{13}N_1 - \frac{N_2}{\tau_2}
In steady state ( rac{dN_2}{dt} = 0), equate the pumping rate from ground state to the spontaneous and stimulated decay rates: W_{13}(N_t - N_2) = \frac{N_2}{\tau_2}
Express the threshold pumping rate W_{th} required to maintain the threshold population N_{2th}: W_{th} = \frac{N_{2th}}{\tau_2 (N_t - N_{2th})}
Relate the critical pumping rate to the absorbed pump threshold power per unit volume P_{th} = W_{th} h \nu_p N_t.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Three-Level Energy Diagram of Ruby
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Energy level diagram showing ground state E<sub>1</sub>, pump band E<sub>3</sub>, and metastable state E<sub>2</sub>. Vertical upward arrow for optical pumping (green light), downward non-radiative transition to E<sub>2</sub>, and downward laser transition (694.3 nm) from E<sub>2</sub> to E<sub>1</sub>.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Illustrates optical pumping and the necessity of depopulating the pump band rapidly to accumulate ions in the metastable state before laser emission occurs.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Frequently asked in TGT/PGT matching questions and descriptive labeling of energy levels.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Ruby Laser Pulse Spiking Output
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: An oscilloscope trace of optical output power versus time, showing a short initial delay followed by a series of chaotic or regular intensity spikes lasting a few hundred microseconds during flashlamp discharge.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Demonstrates relaxation oscillations and dynamic gain switching characteristic of pulsed solid-state lasers where population inversion builds and depletes repeatedly.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Interpreting temporal characteristics of pulsed lasers versus continuous-wave lasers.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Absorption and Fluorescence Spectrum of Ruby
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Graph of optical density or absorption coefficient versus wavelength showing two broad bands in the blue (~400 nm) and green (~550 nm) regions, and a sharp emission line at 694.3 nm (R<sub>1</sub> line).
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Explains why ruby absorbs green and blue pump light and why it appears red by transmitting and emitting red wavelengths.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Questions on optical absorption bands and corresponding emission wavelengths of laser crystals.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the energy of a single photon emitted by a ruby laser operating at a wavelength of 694.3 nm. (Given h = 6.626 x 10<sup>-34</sup> J s, c = 3 x 10<sup>8</sup> m/s)
solution_steps: Identify given values: \lambda = 694.3 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}, h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}, c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}.
Use the photon energy formula: E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}.
Substitute values: E = \frac{(6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}) (3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s})}{694.3 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}}.

solved_numericals.question: A ruby laser rod has a length L = 10 cm and refractive index n = 1.76. Calculate the frequency separation between adjacent longitudinal modes of the optical cavity.
solution_steps: Identify given parameters: L = 0.1 \text{ m}, n = 1.76, c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}.
Use the longitudinal mode frequency spacing formula: \Delta \nu = \frac{c}{2nL}.

solved_numericals.question: Determine the minimum fraction of chromium ions that must be excited to the metastable state to achieve population inversion in a ruby laser, and state why continuous-wave (CW) operation is difficult.
solution_steps: Recall that ruby operates as a three-level laser system where the lower laser level is the ground state (E<sub>1</sub>).
For population inversion, the population of the upper level N<sub>2</sub> must exceed the population of the lower level N<sub>1</sub> (i.e., N<sub>2</sub> > N<sub>1</sub>).
Given the total ion density N<sub>t</sub> = N<sub>1</sub> + N<sub>2</sub>, set N<sub>2</sub> = N<sub>t</sub> / 2 at the threshold condition.
Conclude that more than 50% of the total ions must be pumped into the excited state, requiring immense pump power which causes severe thermal loading and precludes easy CW operation.
solved_numericals.answer: Greater than 50% (> 0.5); CW operation is difficult due to massive thermal dissipation required for continuous threshold pumping of the ground state.

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumes a uniform distribution of Cr<sup>3+</sup> dopant ions throughout the host Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> crystal lattice.
Neglects thermal lensing and refractive index gradients induced by high-power flashlamp pumping.

Limitation: Three-level operation inherently demands high pump power thresholds, leading to high thermal stress and restricting output to pulsed rather than continuous-wave operation under normal conditions.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Ruby laser is a four-level laser system.
common_misconceptions.correct: Ruby laser is a classic three-level laser system.
common_misconceptions.why: The lower laser level is the ground state itself, requiring more than 50% of the total ions to be pumped before inversion is achieved.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The active substance that emits laser light in ruby is the aluminum oxide crystal.
common_misconceptions.correct: The active ions are trivalent chromium (Cr<sup>3+</sup>) impurities.
common_misconceptions.why: The sapphire (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) host crystal only provides a transparent mechanical matrix; optical transitions occur entirely within the chromium ion energy levels.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Ruby lasers easily produce continuous high-power laser beams.
common_misconceptions.correct: Ruby lasers operate primarily in pulsed mode.
common_misconceptions.why: The high threshold requirement generates excessive heat, making continuous-wave operation extremely difficult without cryogenic cooling.

quick_revision: Ruby laser active medium: Cr<sup>3+</sup> ions doped in Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> crystal.
Operating wavelength: 694.3 nm (deep red R<sub>1</sub> line).
Energy level scheme: Three-level laser system.
Pumping mechanism: Optical pumping using a xenon flashlamp.
Population inversion threshold: Greater than 50% of total ions must be excited.
Operation mode: Pulsed laser output with relaxation spikes.
